title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE SPECIAL ACT ON RELIEF AND SUPPORT FOR DAMAGE CAUSED BY THE GYEONGBUK, GYEONGNAM, AND ULSAN MEGAFIRES
title_original: 경북ㆍ경남ㆍ울산 초대형산불 피해구제 및 지원 등을 위한 특별법 시행령
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE SPECIAL ACT ON RELIEF AND SUPPORT FOR DAMAGE CAUSED BY THE GYEONGBUK, GYEONGNAM, AND ULSAN MEGAFIRES

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Special Act on Relief and Support for Damage Caused by the Gyeongbuk, Gyeongnam, and Ulsan Megafires and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Victims)
The term "persons prescribed by Presidential Decree" in item (d) of subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Special Act on Relief and Support for Damage Caused by the Gyeongbuk, Gyeongnam, and Ulsan Megafires (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means persons falling under any of the following:
1. Persons who were engaged in forest fire suppression, rescue, emergency medical services, medical assistance, recovery work, or similar activities in the affected areas (excluding public officials who performed forest fire suppression, rescue, emergency medical services, medical assistance, recovery work, or similar activities as part of their official duties);
2. Persons who were participating in volunteer activities in the affected areas;
3. Persons comparable to those referred to in subparagraphs 1 and 2 for whom the Gyeongbuk, Gyeongnam, and Ulsan Megafires Victim Support and Reconstruction Commission under Article 5(1) of the Act has recognized a causal relationship between the Gyeongbuk, Gyeongnam, and Ulsan Megafires and their physical or mental harm or property damage.

Article 3 (Temporary Housing Facilities)
The term "accommodation facilities and the like prescribed by Presidential Decree" in subparagraph 6 of Article 2 of the Act means facilities falling under any of the following:
1. Temporary housing facilities provided pursuant to subparagraph 1 of Article 4(1) of the Disaster Relief Act;
2. Facilities provided to victims among those falling under any subparagraph of Article 4-2(1) of the Disaster Relief Act.

CHAPTER II VICTIM SUPPORT AND RECONSTRUCTION COMMISSION, ETC.

Article 4 (Composition of the Commission, etc.)
(1) The term of office of members commissioned by the Prime Minister from among the persons referred to in subparagraphs 2 through 6 of Article 6(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to in this Article as "commissioned members") shall be two years and may be renewed consecutively only once. However, the term of office of a member newly commissioned due to the resignation of a member or any other reason shall be the remainder of the predecessor's term.
(2) Even after their terms of office expire, commissioned members may continue to perform their duties until their successors are commissioned.

Article 5 (Duties of the Chairperson)
(1) The chairperson of the Commission (hereinafter referred to as the "chairperson") shall represent the Commission and oversee its affairs.
(2) Where the chairperson is unable to perform the duties of the office due to unavoidable circumstances, a member designated in advance by the chairperson shall perform those duties on the chairperson's behalf.

Article 6 (Disqualification, Challenge, and Recusal of Members)
(1) A member who falls under any of the following shall be disqualified (除斥) from participating in the Commission's deliberations and resolutions:
1. Where the member or the member's spouse or former spouse is a party to the matter under consideration (including the party's officers if the party is a corporation, organization, or the like; hereinafter the same shall apply in this subparagraph and subparagraphs 2 and 4), or is jointly entitled to a right or jointly liable for an obligation with a party to that matter;
2. Where the member is or was a relative of a party to the matter under consideration;
3. Where the member has provided advice, conducted research, performed services (including subcontracted services; hereinafter the same shall apply in this subparagraph), or conducted an appraisal (鑑定) or investigation concerning the matter under consideration. However, this shall not apply where the advice, research, services, appraisal, or investigation was commissioned or requested by a State agency or local government;
4. Where the member or a corporation, organization, or the like to which the member belongs is or was an agent of a party to the matter under consideration.
(2) A party to a matter subject to deliberation by the Commission may apply to the Commission to challenge a member if the member falls under any ground for disqualification set forth in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), or if circumstances exist that make it difficult to expect the member to deliberate and decide impartially, and the Commission shall decide by resolution whether to uphold the challenge. In such cases, the member subject to the challenge shall not participate in that resolution.
(3) A member shall recuse themselves (回避) from deliberations and resolutions on the matter if any of the grounds under paragraph (1) or (2) applies.
(4) The Prime Minister may dismiss a member or terminate the member's commission (解囑) if the member fails to recuse themselves despite falling under a ground for disqualification set forth in any subparagraph of paragraph (1) or being deemed to have circumstances that make it difficult to expect the member to deliberate and decide impartially.

Article 7 (Meetings of the Commission)
(1) Meetings of the Commission shall be convened by the chairperson where the chairperson considers it necessary or at the request of at least one third of the Commission's members in office.
(2) When the chairperson intends to convene a meeting of the Commission, the chairperson shall notify each member of the date, time, place, and agenda of the meeting no later than three days before the meeting. However, where a meeting must be convened urgently, notification may be given no later than the day before the meeting.
(3) A meeting of the Commission shall be opened (開議) with a majority of its members in office present, and resolutions shall be adopted by the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present.
(4) The Commission shall have one secretary to handle its administrative affairs, and the secretary shall be designated by the chairperson from among the employees of the support organization under Article 5(2) of the Act.

Article 8 (Requests for Cooperation from Relevant Public Officials, etc.)
Where the Commission considers it necessary for performing its duties, it may request public officials of relevant administrative agencies, officers and employees of relevant institutions or organizations, and other experts to attend its meetings and state their opinions, or request their cooperation, including the submission of materials or opinions.

Article 9 (Allowances, etc.)
Allowances and travel expenses may be paid, within budgetary limits, to members, public officials of relevant administrative agencies, officers and employees of relevant institutions or organizations, and other experts who attend meetings of the Commission or review matters on its agenda. However, no such payment shall be made where a public official attends a meeting of the Commission or reviews an agenda item in direct connection with that official's duties.

Article 10 (Establishment of an Advisory Group)
(1) The Commission may establish an advisory group if necessary for the efficient performance of its duties.
(2) Members of the advisory group under paragraph (1) shall be commissioned by the chairperson following a resolution of the Commission.
(3) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the advisory group, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) and (2), shall be prescribed by the Commission's rules.

Article 11 (Detailed Rules for Operation of the Commission, etc.)
Matters necessary for the operation of the Commission, other than those prescribed in this Decree, shall be determined by the chairperson following deliberation and resolution by the Commission.

Article 12 (Applications and Procedures for Support Pursuant to the Commission's Deliberations and Resolutions)
(1) A person seeking support under Article 8(1) of the Act shall apply to the head of the Si/Gun/Gu (the head of a Gu means the head of an autonomous district; hereinafter the same shall apply) having jurisdiction over the relevant affected area by submitting a victim support application in attached Form No. 1 with the following documents attached:
1. Documents capable of verifying that the person falls under any of the categories referred to in items (a) through (c) of subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Act and subparagraphs 1 through 3 of Article 2 of this Decree;
2. A copy of the passbook for the account at a financial company or the like to which the support funds are to be paid;
3. A copy of an identification card;
4. A power of attorney (only where the applicant applies on behalf of a victim).
(2) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu who receives an application under paragraph (1) shall verify the following documents through the sharing of administrative information under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act. However, where the applicant and the representative do not consent to verification, the head shall require the documents listed in subparagraphs 1 and 3 through 5 to be attached:
1. Computerized information on family relations registration;
2. A certificate of registered corporate particulars (only where the applicant is a corporation);
3. A certificate of business registration (only where business registration has been completed pursuant to the Income Tax Act, the Value-Added Tax Act, or the Corporate Tax Act);
4. A certificate of the amount of income;
5. A certified copy of a resident registration record (only where the applicant is an individual).
(3) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu may verify the following matters to determine, with respect to the support requested in an application under paragraph (1), whether support for the same items has been or is being provided because of the Gyeongbuk, Gyeongnam, and Ulsan Megafires:
1. The contents of a report of damage from a social disaster under Article 5 of the Regulations on Standards for Bearing Expenses for Relief and Recovery from Social Disasters;
2. The site of damage stated in the application under paragraph (1);
3. Other matters relating to the facts of the damage for which support is requested.
(4) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall forward the application verified under paragraph (3) to the Mayor of Ulsan Metropolitan City, the Governor of Gyeongsangbuk-do, or the Governor of Gyeongsangnam-do (hereinafter referred to collectively as "Mayors/Do Governors"), and the Mayors/Do Governors shall verify the contents of the application and then submit it to the Commission.
(5) Where verification under paragraph (3) shows that the person seeking support has received or is receiving support for the same items with respect to the support requested, the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall notify the applicant that support may be provided excluding that portion pursuant to Article 12 of the Act.
(6) Upon receipt of an application under paragraph (4), the Commission shall deliberate and decide on the support requested by category of support under the Act, formulate support measures under Article 9 of the Act, and notify the relevant Mayors/Do Governors and heads of Si/Gun/Gu of those measures.
(7) Mayors/Do Governors and heads of Si/Gun/Gu who are notified of support measures under paragraph (6) shall formulate and implement support plans for matters under their jurisdiction on the basis of those measures.
(8) Mayors/Do Governors and heads of Si/Gun/Gu shall determine whether to pay support funds and the amounts to be paid on the basis of the support plans formulated under paragraph (7) and notify the applicants of those determinations.
(9) When paying the support funds determined under paragraph (8), Mayors/Do Governors and heads of Si/Gun/Gu shall pay them into deposit accounts designated by the victims. However, where unavoidable circumstances prevent payment into those deposit accounts, support may be provided directly to the victims in cash or in kind.
(10) When paying support funds under paragraph (9), Mayors/Do Governors and heads of Si/Gun/Gu shall inform victims of the payment details, including the purpose and amount of the support funds and the date of payment, through records of transfers to deposit accounts, mobile phone text messages, or other means.
(11) An application under paragraph (1) shall be filed by January 28, 2027. However, where the applicant is unable to apply within that period due to special circumstances, such as residing abroad for a certain period or longer, the application shall be filed within six months from the date on which those circumstances cease to exist.
(12) Matters necessary for support under Article 8(1) of the Act, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (11), shall be prescribed by the Commission's rules.

CHAPTER III SUPPORT FOR VICTIMS, ETC.

Article 13 (Reporting of Victim Organizations)
(1) Where victims form a victim organization under Article 11(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a “victim organization”), the organization shall include at least 10 victims (including the legal representatives of victims; hereinafter the same shall apply in this Article), and at least 1 of those victims shall be selected as a representative.
(2) Victims wishing to form and report a victim organization under Article 11(1) of the Act shall submit a report of establishment of a victim organization in attached Form No. 2, together with the following documents, to the Mayor/Do Governor having jurisdiction over the relevant affected area:
1. Written consents to membership from the members of the victim organization;
2. A roster of the members of the victim organization.
(3) Upon receiving a report under paragraph (2), the Mayor/Do Governor shall verify its contents, issue a certificate of reporting of a victim organization in attached Form No. 3 within 14 days from the date of receipt of the report, and notify the Commission of the reported matters.
(4) Where a report and accompanying documents submitted under paragraph (2) require supplementation, the Mayor/Do Governor may request supplementation, specifying the matters to be supplemented and the period for doing so. In such cases, the time taken for supplementation shall not count toward the period for issuing the certificate of reporting.
(5) Where the representative, office location, or name of a victim organization that has received a certificate of reporting under paragraph (3) changes, the victim organization shall submit a report of changes to a victim organization in attached Form No. 2 to the Mayor/Do Governor. In such cases, the Mayor/Do Governor shall verify the contents of the report, issue a certificate of reporting of changes to a victim organization in attached Form No. 3, and notify the Commission of the reported changes.
(6) Matters necessary for the reporting of victim organizations, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (5), shall be prescribed by the Commission’s rules.

Article 14 (Procedures and Methods for Submission of Opinions by Victim Organizations)
(1) Where a victim organization intends to submit opinions concerning matters on the Commission’s agenda for deliberation and resolution under Article 11(2) of the Act, it shall prepare a statement of opinions in attached Form No. 4 and submit it to the Mayor/Do Governor having jurisdiction over the relevant affected area.
(2) Upon receiving a statement of opinions under paragraph (1), the Mayor/Do Governor shall attach review comments on the victim organization’s opinions to the statement and submit it to the Commission.
(3) Where deemed necessary for reviewing opinions submitted under paragraph (2), the Commission may request the victim organization to submit additional materials concerning those opinions.
(4) Where several victim organizations intend to submit opinions under paragraph (1), they may select one representative to represent those victim organizations.
(5) Matters necessary for the submission of opinions by victim organizations, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (4), shall be prescribed by the Commission’s rules.

Article 15 (Requirements for Joint Farming Organizations)
The area under joint management and the number of participating agricultural business entities required for corporations or organizations that jointly engage in agricultural business under Article 14(2)2 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as “joint farming organizations”) shall be as follows, respectively:
1. Area under joint management: at least 200,000 square meters;
2. Number of participating agricultural business entities: at least 5 farmers (meaning farmers under the Framework Act on Agriculture, Rural Community and Food Industry).

Article 16 (Criteria and Procedures for Support for Joint Farming Organizations)
(1) When providing support under Article 14(3)1 through 4 of the Act to joint farming organizations in affected areas, the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs shall select recipients of support by considering the following matters:
1. The appropriateness of the business plan for joint farming;
2. The operational infrastructure for joint farming;
3. The capacity to carry out the project.
(2) A joint farming organization wishing to receive support under Article 14(3)1 through 4 of the Act shall apply for support to the head of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the location of the organization’s office.
(3) Matters necessary for the criteria and procedures for support for joint farming organizations, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) and (2), shall be determined by the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs.

Article 17 (Criteria and Procedures for Support for Smart Agriculture)
(1) When providing support under Article 14(3)5 and the subparagraphs of Article 14(4) of the Act to joint farming organizations and agricultural business entities in affected areas, the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs shall select recipients of support by considering the following matters:
1. The appropriateness of the business plan related to smart agriculture;
2. The operational infrastructure for smart farms;
3. The capacity to carry out the project.
(2) Joint farming organizations and agricultural business entities wishing to receive support under Article 14(3)5 and the subparagraphs of Article 14(4) of the Act shall apply for support to the head of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the relevant smart farms, facilities related to smart agriculture, and other relevant facilities.
(3) Matters necessary for the criteria and procedures for support for smart agriculture, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) and (2), shall be determined by the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs.

Article 18 (Criteria for Damage Recovery Support for Small Business Owners and Small and Medium Enterprises, Etc.)
(1) Support under Article 15(1) and (2) of the Act for small business owners (meaning small business owners under Article 2 of the Framework Act on Small Business; hereinafter the same shall apply) and small and medium enterprises (meaning small and medium enterprises under Article 2 of the Framework Act on Small and Medium Enterprises; hereinafter the same shall apply) shall cover the following:
1. Damage to or loss of sites and buildings, facilities, equipment, and materials at business premises;
2. Damage to or loss of machinery, equipment, and production, distribution, and processing facilities at business premises;
3. Demolition of damaged facilities under subparagraphs 1 and 2 and disposal of waste.
(2) In addition to the matters prescribed in paragraph (1), criteria for assessing damage and determining support payments shall be determined by the chairperson following deliberation and resolution by the Commission. In such cases, Articles 3 and 4 and the attached Table of the Regulations on Standards for Bearing Expenses for Relief and Recovery from Social Disasters shall be taken into consideration.
(3) A person wishing to receive support under Article 15(1) of the Act shall apply to the head of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the relevant affected area by submitting an application for victim support in attached Form No. 1, together with the following documents:
1. Documents confirming that the person was operating business premises in an affected area at the time of the Gyeongbuk, Gyeongnam, and Ulsan Megafires;
2. A copy of the passbook for the account with a financial company or other institution into which the support payment is to be made;
3. A copy of an identification document;
4. A power of attorney (only where the applicant applies on behalf of a victim).
(4) Upon receiving an application under paragraph (3), the head of the Si/Gun/Gu shall verify the following documents through the joint use of administrative information under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act: Provided, That where the applicant and representative do not consent to verification, they shall be required to attach the documents specified in subparagraphs 2 and 3:
1. A certificate of matters recorded in the corporate register (only where the applicant is a corporation);
2. A certificate of business registration (only where business registration has been made under the Income Tax Act, the Value-Added Tax Act, or the Corporate Tax Act);
3. A certificate of income amount.
(5) Article 12(3) through (10) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the procedures and methods for applying for support for expenses necessary for damage recovery under Article 15(1) of the Act.
(6) Matters necessary for the payment of support payments and other related matters, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (5), shall be prescribed by the Commission’s rules.

Article 19 (Support for Recovery from Damage to Industrial Complexes and Factories)
The State and local governments (hereinafter collectively referred to as the “State and local governments”) may restore the following infrastructure or provide support for restoration costs under Article 16(1) of the Act:
1. Transportation facilities, including roads and parking lots;
2. Distribution and supply facilities, including distribution business facilities and water, electricity, and gas supply facilities;
3. Basic environmental infrastructure, including sewerage systems, waste treatment and recycling facilities, and rainwater storage and utilization facilities.

Article 20 (Criteria for Support for Recovery Costs for Damage to Agriculture, Forestry, and Fisheries)
(1) The scope of damage for which the State and local governments shall provide support for costs under Article 17(1) of the Act shall be as follows:
1. Damage to or loss of agricultural and forestry facilities, and loss of agricultural crops and forest crops;
2. Damage to or loss of livestock breeding facilities, and loss or death of livestock;
3. Damage to or loss of fishing vessels, and damage to or loss of fishing nets and fishing gear;
4. Loss or death of fishery products, damage to or loss of aquaculture facilities, and damage to or loss of salt farms;
5. Reduced growth, toppling, or death of trees;
6. Other damage to facilities, equipment, and crops for agriculture, forestry, and fisheries, as deliberated and resolved by the Commission.
(2) In addition to the matters prescribed in paragraph (1), criteria for assessing damage and determining support payments shall be determined by the chairperson following deliberation and resolution by the Commission. In such cases, Articles 3 and 4 and the attached Table of the Regulations on Standards for Bearing Expenses for Relief and Recovery from Social Disasters shall be taken into consideration.
(3) A person wishing to receive support under Article 17(1) of the Act shall apply to the head of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the relevant affected area by submitting an application for victim support in attached Form No. 1, together with the following documents:
1. Documents confirming that the person was engaged in agriculture, forestry, or fisheries in an affected area at the time of the Gyeongbuk, Gyeongnam, and Ulsan Megafires;
2. A copy of the passbook for the account with a financial company or other institution into which the support payment is to be made;
3. A copy of an identification document;
4. A power of attorney (only where the applicant applies on behalf of a victim).
(4) Upon receiving an application under paragraph (3), the head of the Si/Gun/Gu shall verify the following documents through the joint use of administrative information under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act: Provided, That where the applicant and representative do not consent to verification, they shall be required to attach the documents specified in subparagraphs 2 and 3:
1. A certificate of matters recorded in the corporate register (only where the applicant is a corporation);
2. A certificate of business registration (only where business registration has been made under the Income Tax Act, the Value-Added Tax Act, or the Corporate Tax Act);
3. A certificate of income amount.
(5) Article 12(3) through (10) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the procedures and methods for applying for support for expenses necessary for damage recovery under Article 17(1) of the Act.
(6) Matters necessary for the payment of support payments and other related matters, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (5), shall be prescribed by the Commission’s rules.

Article 21 (Scope of Persons Eligible for Emergency Support, Etc.)
(1) The term “persons prescribed by Presidential Decree among victims” in Article 19(1) of the Act means victims who need livelihood support under Article 9(1)1(a) of the Emergency Aid and Support Act (hereinafter referred to as “persons eligible for emergency support”).
(2) The amount of support for persons eligible for emergency support shall be the amount determined in accordance with the criteria prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of Health and Welfare under the main sentence of Article 2(2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Emergency Aid and Support Act.
(3) The period of livelihood support for persons eligible for emergency support shall not exceed 6 months, the maximum support period under the latter part of Article 10(3) of the Emergency Aid and Support Act.
(4) An emergency support agency under Article 6 of the Emergency Aid and Support Act may, where necessary to support persons eligible for emergency support, request the heads of relevant administrative agencies or relevant persons to submit related materials.
(5) Matters necessary for the criteria, methods, procedures, and other aspects of support for persons eligible for emergency support, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (4), shall be governed by the Emergency Aid and Support Act.

Article 22 (Period for Priority Provision of Child Care Services, Etc.)
(1) The period for priority provision of child care services under Article 19(2) of the Act shall end on January 28, 2031.
(2) The methods and procedures for support for child care services under Article 19(2) of the Act shall be governed by the Child Care Support Act.

Article 23 (Details and Methods of Support for Psychological Counseling, Etc.)
(1) Support under Article 20(1) of the Act shall include identification of persons at high risk of mental health problems, psychological counseling, and support for a return to everyday life.
(2) The heads of relevant central administrative agencies and relevant local governments may provide psychological assessments, psychological counseling, and other assistance for support under Article 20(1) of the Act through mental health welfare centers under Article 15 of the Act on the Improvement of Mental Health and the Support for Welfare Services for Mental Patients, the National Trauma Center under Article 15-2(1) of that Act, regional trauma centers under paragraph (3) of that Article, and other relevant institutions.
(3) The heads of relevant central administrative agencies and relevant local governments may provide support under Article 20(1) of the Act in coordination with support for counseling activities under Article 66(5) of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety.
(4) Matters necessary for support for psychological counseling and other assistance, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (3), shall be prescribed by the Commission’s rules.

Article 24 (Details and Methods of Support for Medical Services, Etc.)
(1) Support for medical services under Article 21 of the Act shall consist of support for the following amounts among the expenses necessary for treatment of physical and mental illnesses and injuries caused by the wildfires and their aftereffects (hereinafter referred to as “injuries, etc.” in this Article): Provided, That costs for which medical expense assistance has been received under other statutes and regulations for the injuries, etc., shall be excluded:
1. The amount borne by the victim under Article 44 of the National Health Insurance Act out of the costs of medical care benefits under Article 41 of that Act;
2. The amount borne by the victim under Article 10 of the Medical Care Assistance Act out of the costs of medical care benefits under Article 7 of that Act.
(2) A person wishing to receive support under Article 21(1) of the Act shall submit an application for support for medical services in attached Form No. 5 to the head of a Si/Gun/Gu, together with the following documents:
1. Medical expense bills and receipts and a detailed itemization of medical expenses;
2. A medical certificate or physician’s opinion confirming that the treatment is for injuries, etc., caused by the wildfires;
3. A copy of the passbook for the account with a financial company or other institution into which the support payment is to be made.
(3) Upon receiving an application under paragraph (2), the head of the Si/Gun/Gu shall decide whether to provide medical support and notify the applicant of the result within 30 days.
(4) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the following expenses essential for the treatment of injuries, etc., caused by the wildfires may be included in support for medical services where the Commission determines the scope of support and other relevant matters through deliberation and resolution:
1. Expenses for items not covered by benefits under Article 41(4) of the National Health Insurance Act;
2. Purchase of assistive devices under Article 51 of the National Health Insurance Act;
3. Expenses for caregiving for victims (in an amount calculated by applying Article 59 of the Enforcement Decree of the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act mutatis mutandis).
(5) Matters necessary for support for medical services, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (4), shall be prescribed by the Commission’s rules.

Article 25 (Period and Methods for Recovery of Support Payments, Etc.)
(1) The term “period prescribed by Presidential Decree” in the portion of Article 22(1) of the Act other than its subparagraphs means the payment deadline specified in a payment notice under paragraph (2) or the deadline specified in a demand for payment under paragraph (3).
(2) When recovering support payments and other assistance under Article 22(1) of the Act, the State and local governments shall issue the person who received support payments a payment notice specifying the fact that payment or assistance was provided, the amount to be recovered and the basis for its calculation, the payment deadline (which shall be set within 30 days from the date of notice), the account for payment, the method for filing an objection, and other relevant matters.
(3) Where the State and local governments recover payments under paragraph (2) and the person required to repay them has not paid the full amount to be recovered by the payment deadline, they shall demand payment, specifying a period not exceeding 30 days.

CHAPTER IV SUPPORT FOR RECOVERY OF AFFECTED AREAS AND LOCAL RECONSTRUCTION

Article 26 (Statutory Policy Projects Eligible for Priority Support)

The term "projects prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 24 (1) 7 of the Act means the following projects:
1. Projects for the sustainable use of timber and the promotion of the timber industry under the subparagraphs of Article 38 of the Act on the Sustainable Use of Timber;
2. Projects for improving production infrastructure, modernizing production facilities, and promoting expansion of their scale under Article 5 (1) 2 and 7 of the Special Act on Assistance to Farmers, Fishers, etc. Following the Conclusion of Free Trade Agreements;
3. Support projects, including projects to promote the production, development, and export of processed fishery products, under the subparagraphs of Article 15 (1) of the Act on Fostering and Support of the Fisheries Food Industry;
4. The following support projects under the Act on the Management and Support of Distribution of Fishery Products (hereinafter referred to as the "Fishery Products Distribution Act" in this subparagraph):
(a) Support projects for the remodeling, repair, etc. of consignment sales markets under Article 22 of the Fishery Products Distribution Act;
(b) Support projects for the modernization of consignment sales markets under Article 22-2 of the Fishery Products Distribution Act;
(c) Support projects for securing sites, installing facilities, etc. for distribution logistics centers for fishery products in consumption areas under Article 48 of the Fishery Products Distribution Act;
(d) Support projects for securing sites, installing facilities, etc. for fishery products distribution hubs in production areas under Article 49 of the Fishery Products Distribution Act;
5. Support projects for the development of technologies related to the aquaculture industry under Article 61 of the Aquaculture Industry Development Act;
6. Support projects for the development of hub areas in agricultural and fishing villages under Article 39 of the Special Act on Improving the Quality of Life of Farmers and Fishers and Promoting the Development of Agricultural and Fishing Villages.

Article 27 (Special Cases concerning Priority Allocation of the Local Extinction Response Fund to Affected Areas)

(1) The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall determine the weighting for allocating the fund under Article 25 (1) of the Act, taking into account the extent of damage, population, financial conditions, etc. of affected areas.
(2) The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall determine the proportion of the fund to be allocated under Article 25 (1) of the Act within five percent of the basic support account under Article 25 (2) 2 of the Framework Act on the Management of Local Government Funds.
(3) When determining the allocation weighting and proportion under paragraphs (1) and (2), the Minister of the Interior and Safety shall hear the opinions of the fund management association under Article 22 (2) of the Framework Act on the Management of Local Government Funds.
(4) When presenting its opinions to the Minister of the Interior and Safety pursuant to paragraph (3), the fund management association shall gather the opinions of the Mayors/Do Governors and the heads of Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over population-decline areas and areas of concern for population decline under the Special Act on Local Autonomy and Decentralization, and Balanced Regional Development.
(5) The Local Extinction Response Fund allocated to affected areas pursuant to Article 25 of the Act shall be used for developing infrastructure and operating systems and programs related to the reconstruction and revitalization of affected areas, responses to local extinction, etc.

Article 28 (Requirements for Special Forest Management Zones)

A special forest management zone designated pursuant to Article 27 (1) of the Act shall meet all of the following requirements: Provided, That subparagraphs 3 and 4 shall apply only where national forests are included:
1. The area of a single special forest management zone shall be at least 3,000,000 square meters;
2. The area for which the forest owners have given their consent shall constitute at least 50 percent of the area of the special forest management zone;
3. The area of national forests incorporated into the zone shall be less than the area of privately owned forests incorporated into the zone;
4. National forests incorporated into the area to be designated shall meet the criteria for the lease of, or permission to use, national forests under Article 21 (1) of the Act on the Management and Administration of National Forests and Article 17 (1) and (3) of the Enforcement Decree of that Act.

Article 29 (Procedures for Designating Special Forest Management Zones)

(1) A person who intends to apply for designation of a special forest management zone pursuant to Article 27 (2) of the Act shall submit an application for designation of a special forest management zone in attached Form No. 6, accompanied by the following documents, to the head of the competent Si/Gun/Gu:
1. A project plan and a plan drawing for the special forest management zone;
2. A topographical map of the proposed special forest management zone showing cadastral boundaries at a scale of 1:25,000 or larger (meaning a cadastral map where no database of topographical maps showing cadastral boundaries has been established in the national land use information system pursuant to Article 12 of the Framework Act on the Regulation of Land Use, or where use of a topographical map is difficult because of discrepancies between the topography and cadastral boundaries);
3. Documents evidencing ownership of, or rights to use or derive profits from, the forest for which designation as a special forest management zone is sought (limited to cases where such rights cannot be verified through a certificate of registered matters concerning land; documents evidencing rights to use or derive profits shall expressly state the scope and duration of those rights);
4. Documents evidencing the consent of forest owners under Article 28, subparagraph 2 (excluding national forests under the jurisdiction of the Korea Forest Service).
(2) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu who receives an application for designation of a special forest management zone under paragraph (1) shall verify the certificate of registered matters concerning land through the joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act.
(3) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu who receives an application for designation pursuant to paragraph (1) shall submit the application for designation of a special forest management zone and the documents specified in the subparagraphs of that paragraph to the Mayor/Do Governor.
(4) A Mayor/Do Governor who receives an application for designation of a special forest management zone pursuant to paragraph (3) shall, where the special forest management zone includes national forests under the jurisdiction of the Korea Forest Service, consult with the head of the national forest management office of the competent regional forest service; where it includes national forests under the jurisdiction of the head of a central government agency other than the Minister of the Korea Forest Service (meaning the head of a central government agency under Article 6 of the National Finance Act), the Mayor/Do Governor shall consult with the competent ministry.
(5) A Mayor/Do Governor may designate the relevant area as a special forest management zone where the project plan is deemed appropriate and consultations on national forests under paragraph (4) have been completed.
(6) Where a Mayor/Do Governor designates the relevant forest as a special forest management zone pursuant to paragraph (5), the Mayor/Do Governor shall give public notice thereof in the official bulletin and notify the applicant, forest owners, and heads of relevant administrative agencies.

Article 30 (Criteria for Support for Special Forest Management Zones)

When providing support under Article 27 (3) and (4) of the Act, the State and local governments shall establish criteria for support for special forest management zones, taking into account the following matters:
1. The size and regional characteristics of the special forest management zone;
2. Whether the support overlaps with support under other statutes or regulations;
3. Other matters that the State and local governments deem necessary for the operation of special forest management zones.

Article 31 (Support for Energy Supply)

(1) The term "support for energy supply prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 28 (1) 5 of the Act means support projects respectively determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Trade and Industry from among energy supply support projects under energy-related statutes and regulations, including the Act on the Promotion of the Development, Use and Diffusion of New and Renewable Energy and the Act on the Safety Control and Business of Liquefied Petroleum Gas.
(2) Support for energy supply under Article 28 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "support for energy supply") shall be provided to the following persons:
1. Victims and residents of affected areas;
2. Other persons for whom the Mayors/Do Governors deem support for energy supply necessary for the recovery of affected areas.
(3) The scope of support for energy supply shall be as follows:
1. Awarding additional points and providing additional subsidies when participating in State support projects related to energy;
2. Subsidizing installation costs and providing priority consulting support when implementing projects for the supply of new and renewable energy;
3. Supporting fuel costs and electricity charges for vulnerable groups and implementing projects to replace equipment with high-efficiency equipment;
4. Providing additional support for liquefied petroleum gas pipeline network projects;
5. Special provisions prescribed in the relevant public notices for support projects respectively determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Trade and Industry pursuant to paragraph (1).
(4) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Trade and Industry shall each determine and publicly notify the scale and methods of support for energy supply within budgetary limits, taking into account the persons eligible for support, the extent of damage, etc.
(5) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Trade and Industry shall each, after consultation with the Mayors/Do Governors of affected areas, publicly notify the procedures and order of priority for support for energy supply, the documents required to apply for support, etc.

Article 32 (Support for Restoration of Waste Treatment Facilities and Equipment)

(1) Facilities and equipment eligible for support for restoration costs under Article 29 (1) of the Act shall be those falling under any of the following subparagraphs:
1. Waste landfill facilities;
2. Facilities for the separate discharge of waste;
3. Facilities for the collection and storage of agricultural waste;
4. Waste collection and transportation vehicles and equipment.
(2) The criteria for support for the costs of restoring waste treatment facilities and equipment under Article 29 (1) of the Act shall be as follows:
1. Costs incurred in restoring the facilities specified in paragraph (1) 1 through 3 (including costs of demolishing damaged facilities, transporting and treating waste, design, construction, and restoration of ancillary facilities);
2. Costs incurred in restoring the vehicles and equipment specified in paragraph (1) 4 (including costs of repair, maintenance, and purchase).
(3) Heads of Si/Gun/Gu who manage and operate waste treatment facilities and equipment and intend to receive support for restoration costs pursuant to Article 29 (1) of the Act shall apply for support to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment, including in their applications the current status of waste treatment in areas affected by the forest fires and matters necessary for restoring waste treatment facilities and equipment.
(4) Heads of Si/Gun/Gu who manage and operate waste treatment facilities and equipment may apply to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment for additional support where additional costs arise in the course of restoration. In such cases, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may provide additional support after reviewing its necessity.

Article 33 (Scope of Hazardous Tree Removal Projects)

(1) The term "hazardous tree removal projects prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 30 (1) of the Act means projects to remove the following trees damaged by forest fires:
1. Trees damaged by forest fires that are likely to cause damage to transportation facilities, such as roads and railways, or to houses, structures, etc.;
2. Trees damaged by forest fires that are likely to cause or spread forest disasters, such as forest diseases and insect pests.
(2) The Minister of the Korea Forest Service shall determine and publicly notify the details of hazardous tree removal projects under paragraph (1).

Article 34 (Procedures for Hazardous Tree Removal Projects)

(1) When notifying forest owners of the implementation of hazardous tree removal projects pursuant to Article 30 (2) of the Act, the Minister of the Korea Forest Service, Mayors/Do Governors, and heads of Si/Gun/Gu shall use the notice of completion of a hazardous tree removal project in attached Form No. 7, stating the following matters:
1. The current status of forest fire damage;
2. The purpose of the hazardous tree removal project;
3. The location, area, and period of project implementation;
4. The number and volume of hazardous trees removed.
(2) The Minister of the Korea Forest Service shall determine and publicly notify details concerning the procedures, etc. for hazardous tree removal projects, other than those prescribed in paragraph (1).

Article 35 (Compensation Criteria for Hazardous Tree Removal Projects)

(1) Compensation for losses under Article 30 (4) of the Act shall be the amount assessed by a certified appraiser or an appraisal corporation under the Act on Appraisal and Certified Appraisers for the following damage caused by hazardous tree removal projects in areas subject to such projects or adjacent areas:
1. The amount of damage to trees;
2. The amount of damage to houses and structures;
3. The amount of damage to agricultural crops, forest products, fruit trees, etc.
(2) The Minister of the Korea Forest Service shall determine and publicly notify matters necessary for the procedures and methods of compensation for losses, detailed criteria for calculating compensation amounts, etc., other than those prescribed in paragraph (1).

Article 36 (Criteria and Procedures for Priority Support for Loan or Subsidy Projects in the Forest Income Sector)

(1) When providing support under Article 31 (1) of the Act, the State and local governments shall establish criteria for priority support for loan or subsidy projects in the forest income sector, taking into account the following matters:
1. The objects and extent of damage;
2. Other matters that the State and local governments deem necessary for priority support for forest income projects in affected areas.
(2) A person who intends to receive priority support for a loan or subsidy project in the forest income sector shall apply for support to the head of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the relevant affected area, attaching documents evidencing the damage.
(3) The Minister of the Korea Forest Service shall determine matters necessary for the detailed criteria for priority support for loan or subsidy projects in the forest income sector, procedures for applying for support, etc., other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) and (2).

Article 37 (Criteria and Procedures for Support for Living Expenses for Farming Households Collecting Forest Products)

(1) The chairperson shall determine the specific criteria for, and amounts of, support for living expenses under Article 31 (2) of the Act following deliberation and resolution by the Commission. In such cases, Articles 3 and 4 of, and the Annex to, the Regulations on Standards for Bearing Expenses for Relief and Recovery from Social Disasters shall be taken into account.
(2) A person who intends to receive support pursuant to Article 31 (2) of the Act shall apply to the Minister of the Interior and Safety by submitting an application for support for victims in attached Form No. 1, accompanied by the following documents:
1. Documents verifying that the person was collecting forest products in an affected area at the time of the Gyeongbuk, Gyeongnam, and Ulsan Megafires;
2. A copy of the passbook for the account with a financial company, etc. into which the support funds are to be paid;
3. A copy of an identification document;
4. A power of attorney (limited to cases where the applicant applies on behalf of a victim).
(3) The Minister of the Interior and Safety who receives an application under paragraph (2) shall verify the following documents through the joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act: Provided, That where the applicant and the proxy do not consent to verification, the Minister shall require that the documents specified in subparagraphs 1 and 3 through 5 be attached:
1. Computerized family relation registration information;
2. A certificate of registered matters of a corporation (limited to cases where the applicant is a corporation);
3. A certificate of business registration (limited to cases where business registration has been made under the Income Tax Act, the Value-Added Tax Act, or the Corporate Tax Act);
4. A certificate of income amount;
5. A certified copy of the resident registration record (limited to cases where the applicant is an individual).
(4) Article 12 (3) through (10) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the procedures and methods for applying for support under Article 31 (2) of the Act.
(5) Matters necessary for the payment of support funds, etc., other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (4), shall be prescribed by rules of the Commission.

Article 38 (Requirements and Procedures for Continued Payment of Forestry and Forest Public-Interest Direct Payments)

(1) Pursuant to Article 31 (3) of the Act, in the case of mountainous land eligible for forestry and forest public-interest direct payments that has been damaged by the Gyeongbuk, Gyeongnam, and Ulsan Megafires, mountainous land registered as eligible for silviculture direct payments under Article 13 (1) of the Act on the Operation of the Direct Payment System for Promoting the Public-Interest Functions of Forestry and Forests may be treated as mountainous land eligible for forest product production direct payments, notwithstanding Article 7 (1) of that Act; or mountainous land registered as eligible for forest product production direct payments under Article 7 (1) of that Act may be treated as mountainous land eligible for silviculture direct payments, notwithstanding Article 13 (1) of that Act.
(2) Pursuant to Article 31 (3) of the Act, a person who carries out activities to restore forestry management infrastructure, such as removing trees damaged by forest fires, on mountainous land eligible for forestry and forest public-interest direct payments that has been damaged by the Gyeongbuk, Gyeongnam, and Ulsan Megafires, and falls under any of the following subparagraphs, may be eligible for forestry and forest public-interest direct payments, notwithstanding Articles 8 and 14 of the Act on the Operation of the Direct Payment System for Promoting the Public-Interest Functions of Forestry and Forests:
1. In the case of engaging in forest product production:
(a) A forester (meaning a forester under the Forestry and Mountain Villages Development Promotion Act; hereinafter the same shall apply) who engages in forest product production using mountainous land with an area of at least 1,000 square meters and either engages in forest product production for at least 30 days per year or has annual sales of forest products harvested through forest product production of at least 600,000 won;
(b) An agricultural corporation (meaning an agricultural corporation under the Act on Fostering and Supporting Agricultural and Fisheries Business Entities; hereinafter the same shall apply) that engages in forest product production using mountainous land with an area of at least 50,000 square meters and either engages in forest product production for at least 30 days per year or has annual sales of forest products harvested through forest product production of at least 22,500,000 won;
2. In the case of engaging in silviculture:
(a) A forester who engages in silviculture using mountainous land with an area of at least 30,000 square meters and engages in silviculture for at least 30 days per year;
(b) An agricultural corporation that engages in silviculture using mountainous land with an area of at least 100,000 square meters and engages in silviculture for at least 30 days per year.
(3) The Minister of the Korea Forest Service shall determine and publicly notify details of the requirements for continued payment of forestry and forest public-interest direct payments under paragraphs (1) and (2).
(4) The procedures for payment of forestry and forest public-interest direct payments under Article 31 (3) of the Act shall be governed by the Act on the Operation of the Direct Payment System for Promoting the Public-Interest Functions of Forestry and Forests.

Article 39 (Special Cases for Affected Areas)
Where the total project cost of a special regeneration plan is changed pursuant to Article 32 (3) of the Act, approval may be obtained from the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport without consultation with the heads of the relevant administrative agencies or deliberation by the local committee, notwithstanding Article 36 (2) of the Special Act on Promotion of and Support for Urban Regeneration.

Article 40 (Area Requirements and Feasibility Assessment Criteria for the Creation of Natural Recreation Forests)
(1) Pursuant to Article 33 (1) of the Act, the following relaxed requirements shall apply to the area for the creation of natural recreation forests and healing forests in affected areas, notwithstanding Article 9-5 (1) 3 of the Enforcement Decree of the Forestry Culture and Recreation Act:
1. Natural recreation forests:
(a) A natural recreation forest created by the State and local governments: The forest area of the proposed site shall be at least 150,000 square meters;
(b) A natural recreation forest created by a person other than the State and local governments: The forest area of the proposed site shall be at least 100,000 square meters. In such cases, where the forest area of the proposed site is at least 100,000 square meters but less than 130,000 square meters, the area of forest whose form and quality are altered by the installation of natural recreation forest facilities (excluding the areas of forest roads, circular trails, walking paths, forest experience courses, and hiking trails installed before the creation of the natural recreation forest) shall not exceed 50 percent of the total area of the natural recreation forest;
2. Healing forests:
(a) A healing forest created by the State and local governments: The forest area of the proposed site shall be at least 250,000 square meters;
(b) A healing forest created by a person other than the State and local governments: The forest area of the proposed site shall be at least 150,000 square meters.
(2) Pursuant to Article 33 (1) of the Act, the feasibility assessment criteria for natural recreation forests and healing forests in affected areas shall be applied with the landscape criteria under Article 9-5 (1) 1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Forestry Culture and Recreation Act relaxed.
(3) Detailed matters concerning the feasibility assessment criteria under paragraph (2) shall be determined by the Minister of the Korea Forest Service.

Article 41 (Support for Implementation of Community Recovery Programs)
(1) Community recovery programs for which all or part of the costs may be subsidized pursuant to Article 34 (2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "programs") shall be as follows:
1. Education related to community recovery;
2. Various forms of counseling and advice for community recovery;
3. Other programs deemed necessary by the State and local governments for the psychological stability of victims and residents of affected areas and for community recovery.
(2) The period for subsidizing costs necessary to implement programs pursuant to Article 34 (2) of the Act shall be three years. In such cases, the State and local governments may extend the support period following deliberation and resolution by the Commission.
(3) Matters necessary for subsidizing costs necessary to implement programs, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) and (2), shall be prescribed by the rules of the Commission.

Article 42 (Scope of Support for Manufacturing Innovation)
(1) The scope of persons eligible for priority support for smart factory deployment projects pursuant to Article 38 (1) of the Act shall be limited to victims that are small and medium enterprises issued a certificate of damage under Article 7 of the Regulations on Standards for Bearing Expenses for Relief and Recovery from Social Disasters, or small and medium enterprises issued a certificate confirming disaster-affected small and medium enterprise status in accordance with standards publicly notified by the Minister of SMEs and Startups.
(2) Where the Minister of SMEs and Startups intends to provide enterprises under paragraph (1) with priority support for smart factory deployment projects under the Act on the Promotion of Smart Manufacturing Innovation of Small and Medium Enterprises pursuant to Article 38 (1) of the Act, the Minister shall establish criteria for preferential treatment, taking into account the scale of the budget, selection methods, and other relevant matters.
(3) Where the Minister of SMEs and Startups establishes criteria for preferential treatment under paragraph (2), the Minister shall inform the Mayors/Do Governors of affected areas of their content.
(4) Matters necessary for the methods and procedures for supporting smart factory deployment projects, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (3), shall be governed by the Act on the Promotion of Smart Manufacturing Innovation of Small and Medium Enterprises.

Article 43 (Requirements for Designating Tourist Complexes)
Requirements necessary for designating tourist complexes under Article 52 of the Tourism Promotion Act pursuant to Article 39 (1) of the Act shall be relaxed and applied in accordance with the following criteria:
1. Area requirement: The total area shall be at least 50,000 square meters but less than 300,000 square meters;
2. Facility requirement: At least two types of facilities, such as facilities for use by tourists, tourist convenience facilities, and tourist accommodation facilities, shall be included.

CHAPTER V DESIGNATION OF FOREST INVESTMENT LEADING DISTRICTS

Article 44 (Proportion of Damaged Mountainous Land in Forest Investment Leading Districts)
"Ratio prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 41 (1) 6 of the Act means 30 percent (20 percent where areas other than mountainous land account for at least 10 percent of the project plan site).

Article 45 (Hearing Opinions When Formulating Forest Investment Leading District Development Plans)
(1) Where a Mayor/Do Governor intends to hear the opinion of the head of the competent Si/Gun/Gu on a leading district development plan under Article 43 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "leading district development plan") pursuant to paragraph (3) of that Article, the Mayor/Do Governor shall require the head of the Si/Gun/Gu to submit a written opinion on the direction of development of the relevant area and the development projects necessary for such development.
(2) Where a Mayor/Do Governor intends to hear the opinions of local residents and experts pursuant to Article 43 (3) of the Act, the Mayor/Do Governor shall prepare a draft leading district development plan, publicly announce its main content in the official bulletin and on the website of the City/Do or through other means, and forward the announced content to the head of the competent Si/Gun/Gu so that it may be made available for public inspection for at least 14 days.
(3) A person who has an opinion on the content of a draft leading district development plan publicly announced under paragraph (2) may submit a written opinion to the Mayor/Do Governor or the head of the competent Si/Gun/Gu during the inspection period under that paragraph. In such cases, the Mayor/Do Governor may have the head of the competent Si/Gun/Gu prepare a written review of the opinions submitted to the Mayor/Do Governor.
(4) The head of the Si/Gun/Gu shall submit to the Mayor/Do Governor the written opinions submitted under the former part of paragraph (3), written reviews of those opinions, and written reviews under the latter part of that paragraph.

Article 46 (Institutions Eligible for Designation as Implementers of Forest Investment Leading Projects)
"Public institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 45 (1) 2 of the Act means the following institutions:
1. The Korea Land and Housing Corporation under the Korea Land and Housing Corporation Act;
2. The Korea Railroad Corporation under the Korea Railroad Corporation Act;
3. The Korea National Railway under the Korea National Railway Act;
4. The Korea Tourism Organization under the Korea Tourism Organization Act;
5. The Korea Rural Community Corporation under the Korea Rural Community Corporation and Farmland Management Fund Act;
6. The Korea Racing Authority under the Korea Racing Authority Act;
7. The Korea Forest Welfare Institute under the Forest Welfare Promotion Act;
8. The Korea Arboreta and Gardens Institute under the Act on the Creation and Furtherance of Arboretums and Gardens;
9. The Korea Forestry Promotion Institute under the Forestry and Mountain Villages Development Promotion Act;
10. The Korea Mountaineering and Trekking Support Center under the Forestry Culture and Recreation Act;
11. The Korea Forest Disaster Safety Technology Corporation under the Forest Disaster Prevention Act.

Article 47 (Deemed Authorization or Permission and Relaxation of Regulations)
(1) "Facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 48 (1) 5 of the Act means infrastructure under subparagraph 6 of Article 2 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act.
(2) Where a Mayor/Do Governor approves an implementation plan or an amendment thereto pursuant to Article 47 of the Act, provisions restricting activities in wetland protection areas under Article 13 (1) of the Wetlands Conservation Act shall not apply pursuant to Article 48 (2) 1 of the Act.

Article 48 (Subjects and Scope of Support for Installation of Infrastructure)
Pursuant to Article 50 (1) of the Act, the State and local governments may directly install the following infrastructure or subsidize the costs of its installation:
1. Transport facilities, such as roads, tracks, and parking lots;
2. Distribution and supply facilities, such as water, electricity, and gas supply facilities and broadcasting and communications facilities;
3. Basic environmental facilities, such as sewerage, waste treatment and recycling facilities, and water pollution prevention facilities;
4. Other facilities deemed necessary by a Mayor/Do Governor for the smooth implementation of forest investment leading projects and the promotion of investment attraction.

Article 49 (Special Cases for Support for Enterprises in Leading Districts)
(1) "Contracts for construction works, goods, services, etc. prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 54 (2) of the Act means the following contracts:
1. Construction contracts: Contracts for general construction and specialized construction under the Framework Act on the Construction Industry, electrical construction under the Electrical Construction Business Act, information and communications construction under the Information and Communications Construction Business Act, and firefighting facility construction under the Firefighting System Installation Business Act;
2. Contracts for the manufacture or purchase of goods: Contracts for the manufacture or purchase of various materials and equipment, machinery, office equipment, computer equipment, and other goods for carrying out construction works under subparagraph 1;
3. Service contracts: Service contracts for engineering activities under the Engineering Industry Promotion Act and for building design and construction supervision under the Certified Architects Act.
(2) Where the implementer of a forest investment leading project (hereinafter referred to as the "project implementer") intends, pursuant to Article 54 (2) of the Act, to grant preferential treatment in contracts under paragraph (1) to persons whose principal business offices are located in the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the forest investment leading district (hereinafter referred to as a "leading district") or in adjacent Si/Gun/Gu (hereinafter referred to as "local enterprises"), the project implementer shall establish the criteria for such preferential treatment in consultation with the Minister of Finance and Economy and the Minister of the Interior and Safety.
(3) The project implementer shall post on its website the criteria for preferential treatment of local enterprises established under paragraph (2), and may request the Mayor/Do Governor to post them on the website of the City/Do. In such cases, the Mayor/Do Governor shall comply with the request unless there is a special reason not to do so.

Article 50 (Special Cases for Application of the Mountainous Districts Management Act in Leading Districts)
(1) Where a leading district is designated, or a zone or other area within a leading district is designated or determined, the authorities with whom consultation is to be conducted according to the category and area of mountainous land, excluding state-owned forests under the jurisdiction of the Korea Forest Service, pursuant to Article 56 (1) of the Act shall be as follows, notwithstanding Article 8 of the Mountainous Districts Management Act and Article 6 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act:
1. Where the area of mountainous land (where consultation on an amendment is sought under the latter part of Article 8 (1) of the Mountainous Districts Management Act, meaning the area of mountainous land to be changed, excluding the area of mountainous land on which consultation has already been conducted; hereinafter the same shall apply in this paragraph) is at least 4 million square meters (at least 2 million square meters in the case of conservation mountainous land): The Minister of the Korea Forest Service;
2. Where the area of mountainous land is at least 500,000 square meters but less than 4 million square meters (at least 30,000 square meters but less than 2 million square meters in the case of conservation mountainous land): The Mayor/Do Governor;
3. Where the area of mountainous land is less than 500,000 square meters (less than 30,000 square meters in the case of conservation mountainous land): The head of the Si/Gun/Gu.
(2) In the case of a forest investment leading project, pursuant to Article 56 (2) of the Act, notwithstanding Articles 12 and 18 of the Mountainous Districts Management Act, mountainous land may be converted or temporarily used to install facilities necessary for a forest investment leading project included in a leading district development plan (excluding solar energy facilities under the Act on the Promotion of the Development, Use and Diffusion of New and Renewable Energy) in conservation mountainous land (excluding areas within mountainous land for public use where conversion or temporary use of mountainous land is restricted under Article 9 (1) of the Mountainous Districts Management Act).
(3) Criteria for permission to convert mountainous land concerning its slope and elevation for forest investment leading projects under Article 56 (2) of the Act shall be as specified in the Annex.

Article 51 (Special Cases for Application of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act in Leading Districts)
Pursuant to Article 57 (1) of the Act, a Mayor/Do Governor may apply the relaxed standards specified in each of the following subparagraphs to the matters referred to therein: Provided, That subparagraphs 2 and 3 shall not apply where land-use areas and land-use districts are deemed to have been designated pursuant to Article 48 (1) 5 of the Act:
1. Restrictions on building construction in land-use areas and land-use districts under Article 76 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act: In the case of a planned management area under Article 36 (1) 2 (c) of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act, public office facilities under subparagraph 14 (a) of Annex 1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Building Act may be constructed in the relevant land-use area, notwithstanding subparagraph 1 (f) of Annex 20 of the Enforcement Decree of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act;
2. Restrictions on building coverage ratios under Article 77 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act: The restrictions may be relaxed to 120 percent of the maximum building coverage ratio under each subparagraph of Article 84 (1) of the Enforcement Decree of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act;
3. Restrictions on floor area ratios under Article 78 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act: The restrictions may be relaxed to 120 percent of the maximum floor area ratio under each subparagraph of Article 85 (1) of the Enforcement Decree of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act.

Article 52 (Methods and Procedures for Evaluating the Operational Performance of Special Cases for Enterprise Support)
(1) Where the head of a relevant administrative agency intends to evaluate the operational performance and other aspects of the special cases under Articles 54 through 60 of the Act pursuant to Article 61 (2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "performance evaluation" in this Article), the head shall formulate an evaluation plan that includes the following matters. In such cases, the head may hear the opinion of the Mayor/Do Governor on the evaluation plan:
1. The basic direction of the performance evaluation;
2. Methods of performance evaluation;
3. Procedures for performance evaluation;
4. Other matters necessary for performance evaluation.
(2) Where the collection or analysis of materials or other activities are necessary to formulate an evaluation plan under paragraph (1), the head of a relevant administrative agency may commission specialized institutions related to evaluation or other relevant entities to conduct surveys or research, or may hear the opinions of experts.
(3) The head of a relevant administrative agency shall notify the Mayor/Do Governor of the evaluation plan formulated under paragraph (1) no later than one year before the notification deadline under Article 61 (2) of the Act.
(4) Where necessary for a performance evaluation, the head of a relevant administrative agency may conduct on-site inspections, interviews with relevant persons, and other activities.
(5) The head of a relevant administrative agency shall comprehensively examine whether to extend or abolish the period of validity of the special cases under Articles 54 through 60 of the Act, matters for institutional improvement, and other relevant matters, and then notify the Mayor/Do Governor of the performance evaluation results and opinions on measures to be taken.
(6) Matters necessary for the methods and procedures of performance evaluation, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (5), shall be determined by the head of the relevant administrative agency.

CHAPTER VI SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 53 (Delegation of Authority and Entrustment of Duties)
(1) Pursuant to Article 64 of the Act, the authority of the Minister of the Interior and Safety concerning payment of livelihood assistance under Article 31 (2) of the Act shall be delegated to the heads of Si/Gun/Gu.
(2) Pursuant to Article 64 of the Act, the State and local governments may entrust the implementation of hazardous tree removal projects under Article 30 (1) of the Act to any of the following persons:
1. Forestry cooperatives or the National Forestry Cooperative Federation under subparagraphs 1 and 4 of Article 2 of the Forestry Cooperatives Act;
2. State-owned forest management teams under Article 23-2 of the Creation and Management of Forest Resources Act and forest business corporations under Article 24 of that Act;
3. Persons registered as engaging in the log production business under subparagraph 1 of Annex 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Sustainable Use of Timbers.
(3) Where the State and local governments entrust duties under paragraph (2), they shall publicly notify the entrusted person and the content of the entrusted duties in the Official Gazette or an official bulletin.

Article 54 (Processing of Sensitive Information and Personally Identifiable Information)
Where unavoidable for performing the following duties, the Commission, the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, and the heads of relevant local governments may process materials containing information on health under Article 23 of the Personal Information Protection Act or resident registration numbers, passport numbers, or alien registration numbers under subparagraph 1, 2, or 4 of Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act:
1. Duties concerning fact-finding investigations under Article 7 of the Act;
2. Duties concerning support following deliberation and resolution by the Commission under Article 8 of the Act;
3. Duties concerning the reporting of victim organizations and the submission of opinions under Article 11 of the Act;
4. Duties concerning support for smart agriculture under Article 14 of the Act;
5. Duties concerning support for the recovery of damage suffered by small business owners and small and medium enterprises under Article 15 of the Act;
6. Duties concerning support for recovery of damage to agriculture, forestry, and fisheries under Article 17 of the Act;
7. Duties concerning support for psychological counseling and other assistance under Article 20 of the Act;
8. Duties concerning medical support under Article 21 of the Act;
9. Duties concerning recovery of support payments and other assistance under Article 22 of the Act;
10. Duties concerning support for forest management in affected areas under Article 27 of the Act;
11. Duties concerning support for energy supply under Article 28 of the Act;
12. Duties concerning support for hazardous tree removal projects under Article 30 of the Act;
13. Duties concerning priority support for forest income projects under Article 31 of the Act.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 36059, January 27, 2026>

This Decree shall enter into force on January 29, 2026: Provided, That subparagraph 11 of Article 46 shall enter into force on February 1, 2026.
